clue.text: Graduate on about fish and 6 in stationery

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so the outer letters wrap around the inner ones

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate's degree
taken as written
a sild is a young herring

explanation.surface: A graduate rambles on about fish and a well-known brand of writing paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On about' looks like rambling, but the graduate and 'on' join and wrap round a young herring. 6 is BOND, and Basildon Bond is a long-standing British brand of writing paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The brand name of the writing paper is completed by the word at 6, so this word is what precedes it on the stationery.

clue.text: Wayward lot — and bars — once seen here?

definitions.text: Wayward lot — and bars — once seen here?

indicators.note: something wayward strays from the proper path, so the letters wander out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gang of young troublemakers, and the bars that held them, in a place now gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a borstal was a British detention centre for young offenders, abolished in 1982, so wayward youths and bars were once found there.
explanation.definitionFit: Delinquent youths were held behind bars in these institutions, which no longer exist, hence 'once'.

clue.text: Gave up bag provided, holding rupees and diamonds? Diamonds

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece sits within the others

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like part of a plant or animal
R is the abbreviation for rupees
'provided' and 'if' both introduce a condition
ice is slang for diamonds
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone surrendered a bag that held money and jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'diamonds' is clued two ways: first by underworld slang, then by the playing-card suit's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To sacrifice is to give something up for a greater cause, so the past tense matches 'gave up'.

clue.text: Pass by circuit on Silverstone's borders

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its edges, so only its outermost letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A racing car laps the edges of the Silverstone track.
explanation.walkthrough: Silverstone is the British Grand Prix motor-racing circuit. 'Pass by' tempts as one phrase, but only 'Pass' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to lapse when it passes or elapses, and a right lapses when it expires.

clue.text: Establishment no-one has a pop at?

definitions.text: Establishment no-one has a pop at?

parts.words: Establishment no-one has a pop at?
parts.note: surface reading: a place nobody ever criticises or attacks
setter's reading: a pop is a father, and the children in this home have none

explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a pop at' is British slang for criticise or attack; here 'pop' is a dad instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A home for children without parents is an institution where nobody has a father.

clue.text: Middle Easterner, furious, escalating a disturbance

indicators.note: escalating means climbing, and in a down entry a climbing word runs from bottom to top

parts.note: mad means very angry
taken as written
to make a scene is to cause a public disturbance

explanation.surface: An angry man from the Middle East stirs up an ever-growing commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Escalating' reads as a disturbance getting worse, but it turns the angry word upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Damascene is a native or inhabitant of Damascus, the Syrian capital, which lies in the Middle East.

clue.text: See 12
Chemical 6 needs energy supplied with current

parts.note: pep is vigour or energy
a tide is a current of water

explanation.surface: A chemical bond requires energy and an electrical current.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is BOND. 'Current' suggests electricity, but here it is a flow of sea water.
explanation.definitionFit: A peptide bond is the chemical link joining amino acids in a protein chain.

clue.text: Peace perhaps increased following meal

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the piece before this word is written second

parts.note: tea is a light afternoon or evening meal in Britain
rose is the past tense of rise, to increase

explanation.surface: Calm grew after everyone had eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: The second piece comes after the meal, so it is written last. 'Peace' looks abstract, but it is a famous rose variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace is a well-known hybrid tea rose cultivar, bred in France in the 1930s, so it is an example.

clue.text: Tactic initially used by City Group

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of the word
Rio de Janeiro is a famous city

explanation.surface: A strategy first adopted by a financial group in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City Group' suggests a bank, but the city is a particular one in Brazil.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a set of three, which is a small group of people or things.

clue.text: Withdraw to the west to secure mushroom baking base?

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside, so one piece goes within another
in an across entry west is leftward, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: to repair to a place is to withdraw there
a cep is a porcini mushroom

explanation.surface: Pull back westward to protect a mushroom used as the base for baking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdraw' here is the old sense of repair, to go off somewhere. Turned round, it splits after its second letter to take in the mushroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible rice paper lines baking trays so macaroons and similar biscuits can be baked on it, making it a base.

clue.text: Check books in German 23 old Ford model chases

indicators.note: to chase is to run behind, so the piece doing the chasing is written after the other

parts.note: 23 is MOTOR, and an Audi is a German motor car
the Model T was an early Ford car

explanation.surface: Inspecting the accounts as an old Ford follows a German motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chases' means the Ford piece runs behind the German one, so it comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official examination of financial accounts, so as a verb it means to inspect them.

clue.text: Moment pastor reconfigured defunct browser?

parts.note: in a trice means in a moment

indicators.note: reconfiguring means setting up in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A vicar briefly fiddles with the settings of an old web browser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browser' suggests software, but here it is an animal that browses on plants, and 'defunct' means extinct.
explanation.definitionFit: This horned dinosaur was a plant-eater, grazing on vegetation, and has been extinct for millions of years.

clue.text: Dictum meum pactum: goodness and wisdom Byron revised over days

parts.note: 'My!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'goodness!'

indicators.note: a revised text has been altered and reworked, so these letters appear in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for days

explanation.surface: A Latin motto, with Byron's wisdom reworked over several days.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' puts the reworked letters above D, so D comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin motto of the London Stock Exchange translates directly into this English promise to keep one's spoken pledge.

clue.text: See seconds binding in some cuts

indicators.note: binding something wraps it round, so the outer letters enclose another piece

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: Look how quickly some meat cuts are tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is the old exclamation for look, and 'in' is used as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Loin is a cut of meat from the back of an animal, so the plural is an example of some cuts.

clue.text: Conservative in group heretical and bigoted

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one letter goes within another piece

parts.note: a set is a group
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
Arianism was an early Christian heresy denying Christ's full divinity

explanation.surface: A Tory in an extremist faction that is unorthodox and intolerant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heretical' could be the definition, but it is the wordplay, naming an ancient Christian heresy; 'bigoted' fits the length.
explanation.definitionFit: Sectarian describes narrow-minded hostility between religious or political groups, a form of prejudice or intolerance.

clue.text: Jaguar car on bend an original model

indicators.note: in an across entry being on something means following it, so the first-named piece goes second

parts.note: an arch is a bend or curve
the E-Type is a classic Jaguar sports car

explanation.surface: A Jaguar on a bend of the road is an original prototype.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' sounds like a car model, fitting the Jaguar, but the definition means a prototype.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is the first pattern or prototype from which later versions are copied.

clue.text: Republic in which Castro deceiving CIA nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, and crazy letters fall out of their sane order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Caribbean republic where Fidel Castro drives the CIA mad by tricking them.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Cold War Cuba, the obvious republic, but the letters of the two names make a Central American one.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica is a sovereign state in Central America governed as a democratic republic.

clue.text: Pupils initially those getting to lecturers?

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so just the opening letter is used

parts.note: first letter of the word
to reach a place is to get to it, so those who do are reachers

explanation.surface: Students first, then the ones who make it to the university teachers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lecturers' suggests academics; the question mark flags a looser sense of people who lecture others morally.
explanation.definitionFit: Preachers deliver sermons and moralising talks, so they lecture their listeners in the scolding sense.

clue.text: 6 saver gets, as yet childless woman tours Italy?

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all round it, so outer letters circle another

parts.note: a woman not yet a mum is pre-mum
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A saver gets a bond, while a woman with no children yet travels round Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is BOND. Premium Bonds are a UK government savings scheme that pays prizes by monthly draw instead of interest. 'Pre-mum' is a jokey coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: A British saver can hold this type of government-backed bond, entered into regular prize draws.

clue.text: Snake appearing in film — through water it sped

indicators.note: to appear in something is to be seen inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's 1982 film
a boa is a large constricting snake

explanation.surface: A snake features in a movie, speeding through water.
explanation.walkthrough: E-boats were fast German torpedo boats of the Second World War, hence the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: These were high-speed motor torpedo craft used by the German navy, now historical vessels that raced across the sea.

clue.text: They believe time served initially limits crime

definitions.note: a clause standing for the plural noun: the people who believe

indicators.note: limits are boundaries on either side, so two letters bound the piece between

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a heist is a robbery

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the leading letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Doing time, they think, keeps crime in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time served' reads as a prison term, but the two words supply separate letters that wrap round the robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: Theists hold a faith in God or gods, so they are people who believe.

clue.text: Law for one with charm taking in grand legal expert

parts.note: appeal is attractiveness or charm

indicators.note: taking something in means admitting it inside, so one letter goes within

parts.note: Jude Law is an English actor, so Law is an example of a Jude
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A lawyer with charisma who is also a rich legal authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Law' looks like the legal field, but it is the actor's surname, and 'for one' asks for his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge who sits in an appellate court reviews lower rulings, so is a senior authority on the law.

clue.text: Gothic writer covering maiden in fruit

indicators.note: covering something means going over and round it, so it ends up inside

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe wrote Gothic tales of horror
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A horror author shields a young woman inside a fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, written M on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pome is the botanical term for a fleshy fruit with a core, such as an apple or pear.

clue.text: Agent 6 in sticky situation occasionally tense

parts.note: to be in a jam is to be in a tricky spot

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A secret agent in a tight spot is sometimes nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is BOND, so the agent is 007.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Fleming's spy is called James Bond, so this is the first name that goes with the surname at 6.

clue.text: Space to reverse round front of traction engine

indicators.note: to reverse is to go backwards, so the word runs from its end
going round something encloses it, so letters sit inside

parts.note: room means space

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Room is needed to back a traction engine round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traction engine' sounds like one machine, but only the first letter of 'traction' is used and 'engine' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor is a machine that turns energy into motion, an everyday synonym for an engine.

clue.text: Bath line's terminus in subterranean railway

parts.note: a tub is a bath

indicators.note: a terminus is the end point of a route, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: The end of a train line from the city of Bath, underground.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English city with a station, but here it is the thing you wash in. The Tube is the everyday name for the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: The London Underground is popularly called the Tube, after its cylindrical tunnels deep below the streets.

clue.text: With no hesitation sea captains will see Poles on ships

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the named letters are dropped

parts.note: a master is the captain of a merchant ship
er is the sound of a hesitation

explanation.surface: Without wavering, ship captains will spot Polish people aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' reads as people from Poland, but it means wooden spars.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainmast is the principal upright spar of a sailing vessel, so these are tall poles found on ships.

clue.text: Universal anger shown about doctor giving offence

indicators.note: being about something means surrounding it, so the outer letters go round

parts.note: U is the film classification for universal
rage is fury or anger
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: Everyone is furious about a doctor who has caused upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two pieces sit side by side and wrap round the doctor. U is the British film certificate for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: To take umbrage is to feel resentment or take offence at a slight.

clue.text: Stones put finally into container that's correct

indicators.note: putting something into another thing places it inside

parts.note: a case is a container

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter is taken

parts.note: last letter of the word
yes affirms that something is right

explanation.surface: Gems are placed in a box, and that's right.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain cat's-eyes are also reflective road studs, but here the gem sense is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's-eye is a gemstone, such as chrysoberyl, showing a narrow band of reflected light like a feline pupil.
